subject: Confirming deployment guardrails & SOC2/BAA evidence — next steps
messages:
From: Katie Reynolds <katie.reynolds@medidial.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: MediDial Health Security Team <security@medidial.com>
Date: 2026-11-18T14:03:00-08:00
Subject: Follow-up from today's discovery — hosting preference and audit asks

Thanks for the call today — helpful breakdown. A couple of clarifying items for our InfoSec/Procurement folks: 

1) For PHI workloads, our security lead needs to know which deployment modes would satisfy our BAAs and what evidence is available for each. Specifically: Hosted (the Redwood public API), Dedicated (reserved GPU pools), or Private (VPC/on-prem).

2) Can you confirm what SOC 2 evidence you can share right away vs what requires an NDA/attestation? We need a short list to present to procurement: (a) SOC 2 Type II report or summary, (b) data flow diagrams for PHI, (c) encryption key management description, (d) retention/logging options.

We'd like a bulleted response we can hand to our security reviewer. Also planning for a quick follow-up call early next week (Mon/Tue) — would prefer someone technical on the call to discuss Dedicated capacity SLAs.

Thanks,
Katie Reynolds\Director of Product Integrations\MediDial Health
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
To: Katie Reynolds <katie.reynolds@medidial.com>
Cc: MediDial Health Security Team <security@medidial.com>
Date: 2026-11-18T16:11:00-08:00
Subject: RE: Follow-up from today's discovery — hosting preference and audit asks

Katie — great to speak earlier. Below is a concise, handoff-ready summary you can share with your security/procurement teams. I copied the items we discussed and next steps.

Short summary by deployment mode:
- Hosted API (fastest onboarding): supports PHI under our BAA offering for customers who accept our shared-hosting controls. Evidence available: SOC 2 summary (redacted), encryption-at-rest/in-transit description, data retention and access controls. Note: Hosted customers share multi-tenant capacity; dedicated tenancy is not guaranteed for hosted.
- Dedicated (reserved capacity): recommended for customers prioritizing tenancy isolation and predictable throughput. Evidence available: SOC 2 summary + architecture whitepaper, isolation diagram, capacity SLAs. Can provide customer-specific deployment topology and can be scoped into BAA terms.
- Private VPC / On-prem: for the strictest controls (air-gapped or customer-managed infra). Evidence available: full SOC 2 report under NDA, deployment runbook, KMS/HSM integration docs, and on-prem installation checklist. This path requires additional procurement lead time (typically 6-10 weeks for onboarding).

SOC 2 / evidence breakdown (what we can share now):
- redwood-soc2-summary.pdf (attached) — executive summary of controls suitable for initial review.
- Encryption + Key Management — short write-up available; for full KMS attestation we require an NDA.
- Audit logs / retention options — we provide per-tenant log export for Dedicated and Private; Hosted offers aggregated logs and token-level billing traces.

Next steps I propose:
1) I attached the SOC 2 executive summary and a high-level options worksheet.
2) Marissa (cc'd) can provide an indicative quote for Dedicated vs Private with expected lead times.
3) If MediDial wants the full SOC 2 Type II, sign a mutual NDA and we'll route the report through our security team (we can do this in 48–72 hours once NDA is in place).

Availability: I'm free Mon 11/22 10:00–13:00 PT or Tue 11/23 09:00–11:00 PT. Who should join from your side?

Cheers,
Jonas Weber\Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-11-19T09:02:00-08:00
Subject: FW: Follow-up from today's discovery — hosting preference and audit asks

Looping you both in — MediDial (Katie) wants the short, shareable breakdown for InfoSec and procurement and wants a technical presence on a call early next week to discuss Dedicated SLAs and evidence.

Ask for Karthik: can you confirm the specific artifacts we can provide for Dedicated vs Private? Bullet list for: architecture/topology diagram, per-tenant audit export, SLA latency p95 targets, and any customer-provided KMS integration constraints. Also include expected onboarding lead time for Dedicated pools vs Private VPC (days/weeks).

Ask for Marissa: please prepare an indicative pricing worksheet (no formal quote) for: 
- Hosted (with BAA) — monthly usage estimate and any unit discounts for committed spend
- Dedicated (monthly reserved GPU pools) — 3 sizing options and lead times
- Private VPC — base integration fee + recurring platform fee estimate and sample contract timeline

Attachment to include with outward reply: redwood-soc2-summary.pdf and the indicative pricing spreadsheet once ready (proposed-deploy-options-quote.xlsx).

Karthik/Marissa — can you send your bullets back by EOD so I can send MediDial a consolidated reply first thing 11/20?

Thanks,
Jonas
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Katie Reynolds <katie.reynolds@medidial.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-11-20T09:22:00-08:00
Subject: RE: Follow-up from today's discovery — hosting preference and audit asks

Hi Katie — quick consolidated reply and next steps below. Thanks for putting the asks together.

Key artifacts (attached):
- redwood-soc2-summary.pdf — executive SOC 2 controls summary (no NDA required)
- proposed-deploy-options-quote.xlsx — indicative cost/lead-time worksheet (internal numbers, for planning only)

Short answers (you can paste these into your security ticket):
- Hosted + BAA: Acceptable for many PHI use cases; we offer a customer BAA. Evidence: SOC2 exec summary, encryption overview, support for token-level logs. Lead time: immediate onboarding (hours-days).
- Dedicated: Stronger tenancy isolation and per-tenant audit exports. Evidence: SOC2 summary + architecture diagram + per-tenant log export. Lead time: 2–4 weeks for capacity allocation and onboarding (faster if committing to a 3–6 month pool).
- Private VPC / On-prem: Highest control, full-options for KMS/HSM. Evidence: full SOC2 Type II under NDA, deployment runbook, and on-prem checklist. Lead time: 6–10 weeks depending on customer infra and legal.

Procurement asks and next steps:
1) If you want the full SOC2 report, please send us a signed mutual NDA and we'll route the report (we can do that within 48–72 hours).
2) If you'd like an internal technical call about Dedicated sizing and SLAs, Jonas and Karthik can join Mon 11/22 at 10:30 PT. Please confirm attendees.
3) If you want pricing scenarios vs expected monthly token throughput, we can finalize the worksheet after a short sizing form (3–5 questions) — I can send that now if helpful.

Attachment stubs: [attachment: redwood-soc2-summary.pdf (pdf)], [attachment: proposed-deploy-options-quote.xlsx (xlsx)]

Best,
Marissa Cole\Account Executive\Redwood Inference\Phone: (555) 555-0123
